Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The sign is at the north junction, where the loop meets Quarry Spur, about half a mile from the lower parking lot. Its face is faded enough that visitors have to stop close to read the route names, and the lower right corner has split away from the backing. The post is still upright, so this is a sign replacement rather than a request to close or reroute the trail. I first recorded the damage on May 6, during the regular morning walk-through.

Malik Chen, our maintenance technician, went to the junction on May 8 and measured the existing post and panel. He noted that the post is four inches wide, the panel is twenty-four inches by thirty-six inches, and the mounting holes are spaced six inches apart. Malik also checked the hardware and told me that two of the four bolts are rusted, while the other two can probably be reused if they come out cleanly. He took photographs from the trail approaches and one close photograph of the broken corner. I have attached those four photographs to the work request, along with his measurements. Malik did not remove the old panel or loosen the bolts; he said he wanted the replacement panel on site first so the junction would not be left without a readable sign.

When i spoke with Malik afterward, he said, “The post feels solid when I push it, but I could not see below the soil line.” I have kept that distinction in the request because we have no information about the buried part of the post. The soil around the base was damp, and there was no visible leaning, cracking, or exposed footing. These observations do not confirm the post is sound below ground. If the crew finds movement when the old panel comes off, the work may need to include a post assessment rather than only a panel swap. I am not asking Jo to authorize a post replacement now; I am asking Jo to schedule the sign work and let the crew report what it finds.

The panel text should match the current Cedar Loop map. It needs to show “Cedar Loop,” “Quarry Spur,” and the lower parking lot symbol, with the loop marked as 2.4 miles. The existing sign says 2.3 miles, but the map revised last October gives the route as 2.4 miles. The map is the reference we have been using at the visitor desk and on the printed trail sheets. Malik photographed the junction from both directions, and the pictures show that the trail names are still correct; only the distance needs updating. Please have the replacement use the same dark green background and white lettering as the other signs installed along Cedar Loop, rather than a new color scheme. I do not have a final panel proof to attach yet.

1. Work requested from Jo Bell: reserve a crew to remove the damaged Cedar Loop panel at the north junction and install a replacement panel using the dimensions and current map information above. Please include the rusted bolts in the crew’s materials check, since Malik could not confirm that they will be reusable.
2. Work already completed by Malik Chen: measure the post and panel, inspect the visible hardware, and take four photographs. He has not taken down the sign, ordered a panel, or inspected the buried post.
3. Information still needed at the site: once the old panel is removed, the crew can check whether the post moves and whether the mounting holes are usable. I can provide the October map excerpt if the panel shop needs it, but no shop proof or installation date has been confirmed.

The junction has enough space for a crew vehicle to pull off the trail, but the vehicle should not block the narrow walking approach from Quarry Spur. The closest level place to unload is beside the trail map case, roughly thirty feet west of the sign. That case is fixed in place and is not part of this repair. On May 8, Malik found no fallen limbs or other obstruction between the map case and the junction. The ground becomes soft after rain, however, and the work area is shaded for most of the morning. I am including these details so Jo can pass them along when a crew date is discussed, not to suggest that access has already been arranged.

There is a second sign at the south entrance to Cedar Loop, but it is legible and does not need replacement. Its panel is the same size and color as the north junction sign, which may help the crew identify the intended style. It is mounted on a different post, and Malik did not measure or inspect that post during this visit. The visitor desk has had two questions this month about the north junction sign, both from people checking whether Quarry Spur was part of Cedar Loop. I recorded those questions in the visitor log; neither report described someone getting lost or needing assistance. They help explain why the faded labels are becoming a practical concern, but they do not change the requested scope.

If the ground is still saturated on the crew’s scheduled day, please have the crew avoid digging or applying force to the post until the area is firm enough to work safely. The panel can be carried to the junction for a visual fit check, but that check would not establish the condition below ground. If the post shifts during removal, I want the crew to stop the panel installation and report the movement to Jo before proceeding with any additional work. If it stays firm and the holes accept the replacement hardware, the crew can complete the panel swap as requested. I am asking Jo Bell to coordinate that distinction with the crew; I am not recording a crew date or a finding about the post in this account.

Please use this account, Malik’s measurements, and the attached photographs when deciding which crew and panel details to send forward. I can bring the October map excerpt to the district office or email a scan if Jo needs it for a panel order. At present, I have not requested a print run, and no replacement panel has been made.
